title: Canonical source tensor normalization and completion unit
statement: Fix $P$, a finite coefficient field $E$, a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of schemes over the fixed base field, and $d\in\mathbf N$. SourceNormalization records the existing representative-normalized ordinary/completed tensor coordinates, K-flatness of the degree-zero Tate line $(d)$, and the natural isomorphism from the exact-twist pullback/shift source to its ordinary derived-tensor presentation. For every constructible input and every K-flat representative of its pullback this isomorphism is fixed by the exact-derived counit, the site tensor isomorphism, the total-single collapse and the published K-flat tensor comparison. completedSourceObject is the published constructible pullback, completed tensor with that same Tate line, and shift. sourceCompletion is the actual tensor completion unit applied to the pullback and line and then shifted. None of these maps is defined using gamma or an exceptional comparison. Built from [def-pur-conventions], [def-sp-field-extension-canonical-source-word], [def-sp-twisted-pullback-reduction-data], [def-sf-integral-system-canonical-bridge], [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. The unshifted completedTensorObject is explicit; completedSourceObject uses the inherited integral shift. sourceCompletion includes the canonical shift comparison of the full-subcategory inclusion.
